title.narrative: 2.2. Number of territories that estimate the contingent liability for disasters using the improved methodology adapted to the subnational level.

comment.narrative:
The MHCP and the WB are providing support to the municipalities of Dosquebradas and Bogotá for the quantification of contingent liabilities due to disasters. Cali and Medellin are interested in doing the same once their DRF strategies are approved (during the second half of 2025).
Dosquebradas is making progress in applying the methodology supported under this PA, and has prioritized nine risk scenarios for its implementation: flood, flash flood, mass movements, technological risk, damage to vegetation cover, forest fire, volcanic ash, biological risks (post-COVID) and earthquakes.
Bogota is holding inter-institutional meetings (IDIGER-SHD) to define how to apply the methodology, including by modelling losses due to seismic risk, mass movements, flood and torrential floods.

title.narrative: 2.1. Number of annual Medium-Term Fiscal Frameworks applying the improved methodology to quantify contingent liabilities in the event of disasters.

comment.narrative: The MHCP has established inter-institutional working groups (with the UNGRD, SGC, WB and MinAmbiente) to identify, standardize and model the information for the quantification of contingent liabilities due to disasters. The working groups are currently exploring the availability of information at the relevant entities and information needs going forward, as well as possible mechanisms for its collection, verification and standardization.

title.narrative: 5. Percentage of road infrastructure projects that incorporating geotechnical corridor analysis in their planning

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Transport is in the process of revising the Geotechnical Corridor Guide, which was developed with technical support from the WB. The objective is to formally adopt the guide and ensure its systematic application to infrastructure projects managed by Invias, thereby strengthening geotechnical risk management in the sector.

title.narrative: 3. National Information System on Climate Change (SNICC) operation guide adopted.

comment.narrative: The Technical Committee of the SNICC has approved the Operating Regulations and endorsed three of the nine protocols needed to finalise the SNICC Operating Guide: administration, planning and decision-making.

title.narrative: 7. Number of people benefiting from resilient public hospitals.

comment.narrative: To enhance access to quality healthcare in resilient facilities, construction of three new hospitals is underway in Soacha, Manaure, and La Uribia. Additionally, the resilience and preparedness of eight existing public hospitals are being evaluated to ensure compliance with established resilience standards. These efforts aim to strengthen the health sector's capacity to provide uninterrupted services during adverse events.

title.narrative: 4.2. Percentage of municipalities reporting the incorporation of gender-specific actions in their risk management instruments (municipal plans and emergency response strategies)

comment.narrative: Of the 1,103 municipalities covered by the Strategic Framework for Risk Management, 645 have completed their reports. - 199 municipal plans-PMGRDs have incorporated a gender approach, representing 18% of municipalities nationwide. - 183 Emergency Response Strategies -EMREs have incorporated a gender approach, representing 16.6% of all municipalities in the country.

title.narrative: 6. Number of actors in the national tourism sector benefiting from projects that contribute to environmental sustainability, the circular economy and climate change adaptation and mitigation

comment.narrative: The project, 'Improving the Sustainability and Competitiveness of MSMEs in the Tourism Sector', has benefited 100 service providers in the tourism sector. In addition, 245 tourist accommodation providers participated in Circular Economy workshops, and are now required to develop action plans to define strategic interventions and priority investments to strengthen their sustainability and competitiveness.

title.narrative: 1.2. Guidelines for guarantees and counter-guarantees for subnational contingent credit operations approved.

comment.narrative: Although there is a general legal framework for credit operations at the subnational level, the GoC is evaluating what specific adjustments are required for contingent credit operations. To that end, coordinating meetings are expected to be held between the sub-directorates of the MHCP in the coming months to determine the necessary actions to move this indicator forward.

title.narrative: 4.1. National Strategy for Coordination for Adaptation to Climate Change of Human Settlements and Resettlements approved by Presidential Decree.

comment.narrative: The final versions of the required regulatory documents — the Memorandum of Justification, the Supporting Technical Document and the Decree — are currently under preparation and review. These documents are being carefully drafted and discussed among relevant stakeholders to facilitate their timely approval and effective implementation. This process is critical to ensuring a robust regulatory framework that supports the project's objectives
